text: Your website's contact form could be broken right now, and you'd never know.
A broken form doesn't show an error. It just goes quiet.
The customer hits send, sees a thank you message, and waits for a call that never comes.
Usually it's one of three things.
One: it sends to an old email address, like the one for a staff member who left.
Two: the messages land in spam, because your inbox doesn't trust the address the website sends from.
Three: a plugin or website update broke the form, and nobody checked.
The fix takes two minutes. Once a month, fill in your own form from your phone.
Check it arrives in your main inbox, not spam.
And put your phone number right next to the form, so customers always have a backup.
